newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian bonds close weak on U.S. risks.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian bonds close weak on U.S. risks.

text.p: *Australian bonds closed weak after breaking several technical support levels, triggered off by further weakness in U.S. Treasuries on Wednesday.
*Spreads to the dollar bloc blow out sharply.
Australian bonds closed weak after breaking several technical support levels on futures, triggered off by further weakness in U.S. Treasuries on Wednesday as the fear of a Fed rate hike intensified.

Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan, who has already warned of a pre-emptive tightening, is due to testify to the Joint Economic Committee about monetary policy and interest rates later today, and markets globally will be hanging on his every word for clues on policy.
However, some traders believe his speech will be low key given that the Federal Open Market Committee meets next week.
The 10-year benchmark bond yield spiked through 8.0 percent and to its highest level since October last year as futures attracted hedge fund selling.

Comments by Reserve Bank governor Ian Macfarlane that he expected underlying inflation to remain close to the current level of 2.1 percent for the foreseeable futures had limited impact in a market already predicting a fairly benign outlook.
However, despite the size of today's move, which saw June 10-year bond futures slice through support at 91.950 and 91.900, turnover was fairly low, and physical flows remained minimal, traders added.

Local weakness saw spreads to the dollar bloc blow out sharply with the Australian 10-year margin to the U.S. testing resistance at around 130 basis points. However, this was based on New York closing levels with Asian trading in U.S. securities halted due to today's holiday in Japan.
